heroSub: 10 hotels in Chiang Rai city we've reviewed in depth — quiet luxury resorts on the Kok River that stay close to town, Lanna boutiques downtown within walking distance of the Walking Street, warm family guesthouses, and budget stays that still have a pool. Prices from around ฿450–3,500/night.
introH2: 🏙️ What kinds of hotels are there in Chiang Rai city, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Chiang Rai city is small and compact, but the range of places to stay is wider than many people expect — and that's exactly why choosing a hotel here takes a bit of care. On one side are the luxury resorts along the Kok River that sell peace and quiet, with big gardens, riverside pools, and a spa, but you have to drive into town every time. On the other side are the downtown hotels and guesthouses within a few minutes' walk of the Walking Street, the Night Bazaar, and the famous khao soi shops, but with no river view. And then there's the group of budget stays that start under a thousand baht yet still have a pool to cool off in. A lot of people book on brand name or pretty photos alone, only to find later that the location or the vibe doesn't match their style of trip. This article rounds up 10 hotels in Chiang Rai city we've reviewed in depth — riverside on the Kok, downtown, and around the Rop Wiang area — and every one comes from reading real guest reviews, with the upsides and the honest caveats laid out, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Chiang Rai has no metro and no convenient city public transit. The main ways to get around are Grab, songthaew (red trucks), or renting a car or motorbike to drive yourself. Getting here: by plane, you land at Chiang Rai's Mae Fah Luang Airport (CEI), about 1 hour 20 minutes from Bangkok, then around 10–20 minutes by car into the center. By bus, it's about 11–12 hours from Bangkok, or about 3 hours connecting from Chiang Mai, arriving at the central bus terminal. The areas in this article: Kok riverside (the Rop Wiang / Rim Kok area) — quiet, resorts with river and garden views, about a 5–10 minute drive into town. Downtown (Wiang sub-district) — walking distance to the Walking Street, Night Bazaar, and Clock Tower, good if you don't have a car. The Rop Wiang area / near Central Plaza — quiet outskirts, close to the airport, good if you drive yourself.

entries.name: Le Meridien Chiang Rai Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Kok riverside·Rop Wiang · 10 min to town and airport
tags: 🏊 300 sq m pool with river view
entries.addr: 221/2 Moo 20, Kwaewai Road, Robwieng, Mueang Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: If we're going to open the list with the resort that fits best for anyone who wants a riverside escape without cutting themselves off from town, plenty of reviews give it to Le Meridien Chiang Rai Resort — a 5-star boutique resort in the Marriott group on roughly 26 rai along the Kok River in the Rop Wiang area, open since 2008 and still holding a high score of 9.3. What makes people fall for it is the feeling of being a resort set apart from the bustle, even though it's just a roughly 10-minute drive to the Clock Tower, the Night Bazaar, and Mae Fah Luang Airport. The highlight reviews mention most is the roughly 300-square-meter outdoor pool that stretches along the Kok River, prettiest in the soft late-afternoon light, paired with the Favola Italian restaurant that locals drive over to eat at, and the Parvati Spa that many reviews call the best in Chiang Rai. Rooms start at the Deluxe at around 53 sq m, surprisingly spacious for an entry-level room, and every room has a balcony. What draws the most consistent praise is the service — the staff score on Booking is around 9.5, and reviews describe the team the same way: warm, remembering guests' names from day one, until many feel like regulars. The honest caveats from the reviews: the area around the resort is residential with nothing to walk to, so you have to call a car every time you leave; some parts of the building are starting to show their age given the opening year; and meal prices at the resort run higher than restaurants in town. Best for couples, families, and anyone who wants to use the resort as a base for driving out to Wat Rong Khun and Wat Rong Suea Ten. Rooms from around ฿3,500/night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a riverside room (River View) or the Grande Deluxe for a balcony over the Kok River and the morning mist in winter. Book a table at Favola ahead, especially on weekend nights, because locals often fill it up.
pros: Quiet riverside resort on the Kok, yet 10 minutes to town and the airport
Warm staff service, staff score around 9.5 on Booking
300 sq m riverside pool, lovely in the evening · Favola Italian restaurant locals come to
Spacious rooms from 53 sq m, every room with a balcony · Parvati Spa
cons: No walkable area around the resort, you have to call a car every time you go out
Building opened in 2008, some parts starting to show age (per reviews)
Resort meal prices run higher than restaurants in town

entries.name: Nak Nakara Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.3 · 116 reviews · among Tripadvisor's top tier
entries.badge: 🎨 Lanna downtown · walk to the Walking Street
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Uttarakit Road·downtown · 3 min walk to the Walking Street
entries.addr: 661 Uttarakit Road, Wiang, Mueang Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: If you want to stay right in the center of Chiang Rai where everything is walkable, but still want a pool and a quiet garden to unwind in after a full day out, Nak Nakara Hotel is the 4-star boutique many people book again. It's a roughly 70-room hotel that plays with a contemporary Lanna identity in bright tones, on Uttarakit Road next to the Hilltribe Museum, opened in 2011 and renovated in 2016, scoring 9.3 from around 116 reviews on Trip.com. The number-one selling point is the location — a roughly 3–5 minute walk to the Chiang Rai Walking Street (open Saturday nights), with the Night Bazaar and the golden Clock Tower a roughly 10–15 minute walk away, so you can get around town almost without a car. What sets it apart from typical downtown stays is the outdoor pool in a green garden with a separate kids' pool, and the service guests mention with the biggest smile: free bikes to borrow for riding around the old town. Breakfast also gets plenty of praise — some international reviews even call it the best hotel breakfast of their Thailand trip. The honest caveats: hot water is inconsistent in some rooms, Wi-Fi is weak in some spots, rooms on the Uttarakit Road side pick up traffic noise during the day, and after several years open some parts are starting to show wear. Best for couples, families, and anyone who mainly wants to explore the town on foot, from around ฿1,500/night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Borrow a free bike to ride to the Walking Street, the old-town temples, and the cafes nearby — more fun and cheaper than calling a car. If you're sensitive to noise or like a bright room, ask for an upper floor or a room facing the garden/pool, and test the hot water at check-in.
pros: Downtown location, walk to the Walking Street and Night Bazaar
Bright, distinctive Lanna design, not like a chain hotel
Has a pool in the garden and free bikes to borrow
Varied breakfast many reviews call a highlight of the trip
cons: Hot water inconsistent in some rooms · Wi-Fi weak in some spots
Rooms on the road side pick up traffic noise during the day
Open for several years, some parts starting to show wear

entries.name: Le Patta Hotel Chiang Rai
entries.badge: 🏆 Highest score in this article · free snacks all day
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phaholyothin Road·Wiang sub-district · 100 m to the Walking Street
tags: ☕ Free snacks and drinks all day
entries.addr: 610 Phaholyothin Road, Wiang, Mueang Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: Among the downtown hotels in Chiang Rai, if you measure by review score, Le Patta Hotel Chiang Rai is the highest scorer in this article at 9.6 from 783 reviews on Trip.com, and Tripadvisor ranks it #4 of 107 hotels in Chiang Rai. It's a compact 4-star boutique with just 40 rooms, opened in 2013, focused on personal attention and a warm atmosphere, on Phaholyothin Road in Wiang sub-district, right in the center. A top selling point is the location — only about 100 meters from the Saturday Walking Street, with the Chaloem Phrakiat Clock Tower and the Night Bazaar a few minutes' walk away. But what reviews mention most and what wins guests over is the lounge corner with free coffee, tea, snacks, and drinks all day, from morning till evening, sometimes with sandwiches in the afternoon, paired with an outdoor saltwater pool with a koi pond and a green, shady garden that's quieter than you'd expect for a downtown hotel. Service is the heart of this place — several staff get singled out for praise by name, and the service and cleanliness scores on Trip.com are around 9.7–9.8. The honest caveats: the front view faces the big Phaholyothin Road so it isn't pretty, the beds are on the soft side for people who like a firm mattress, and the pool is rather small for anyone who wants to swim seriously. Best for couples, small families, and travelers who want to stay downtown on an affordable budget, from around ฿1,100/night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Make the most of the freebies — the snacks and drinks at the lounge all day, the bikes for riding around town, and the non-alcoholic minibar in the room. If you care about the view and quiet, ask for a room looking out over the pool and garden at booking, since the front rooms face the big road.
pros: Highest score in this article 9.6 · Tripadvisor #4 of 107 hotels
Free snacks and drinks all day at the lounge (the most-praised point in reviews)
Just 100 m from the Saturday Walking Street, walk to the market and Clock Tower
Saltwater pool with a koi pond and shady garden · warm, easygoing service
cons: Front view faces a big road, not pretty
Beds on the soft side for people who like a firm mattress
Small pool, better for a dip than serious swimming

entries.name: The Riverie by Katathani
entries.badge: 🛝 Family resort · water park on site
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Kok riverside·downtown · 1.7 km from the Clock Tower
tags: 🛝 The River Splash water park + kids' club
🌆 The Peak rooftop with city view
entries.addr: 1129 Kraisorasit Road, Wiang, Mueang Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: Chiang Rai doesn't have many large luxury resorts that sit right on the Kok River in the center of town like this — The Riverie by Katathani is a resort in the Katathani group (the same brand as the famous resort at Kata, Phuket), built on more than 50 rai, with 271 contemporary Lanna-style rooms all newly renovated. What sets it apart from the other luxury resorts in Chiang Rai is that it gets both — the riverside atmosphere with mountain views, yet it's only about 1.7 kilometers from the Chiang Rai Clock Tower, so in the evening you can head out for good food at the Night Bazaar and come back to sleep easily. Tripadvisor ranks it #2 of 107 hotels in Chiang Rai, scoring 9.4 from 945 reviews. The highlight families choose it for is The River Splash water park with slides and a kids' zone, plus a kids' club — children often won't get out of the pool all day — paired with The Peak Wine & Grill rooftop with a wide view of the river, mountains, and city lights, good for a special dinner. Breakfast at Blossom and room cleanliness also get plenty of praise, and the value-for-money score on Booking is around 9.5. The honest caveats: it's a large resort and gets lively on long holidays, the quality of meals other than breakfast is inconsistent, sun loungers around the pool are limited on busy days, and soundproofing between rooms may not be enough for light sleepers. Best for families with children and anyone who wants a luxury riverside resort with a water park, from around ฿2,600/night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose a Deluxe River room or a higher floor on the river side for views of the Kok River, morning mist, and more quiet. If you're with family, go down to grab a poolside lounger early on busy days, and book a table at The Peak ahead, especially around sunset.
pros: Riverside resort on the Kok in the center, 1.7 km from the Clock Tower, both view and convenience
The River Splash water park and kids' club are a big hit with children, great for families
Spacious newly renovated rooms · The Peak rooftop with a 180-degree city view
Strong value for money on Booking, around 9.5
cons: Large 271-room resort, lively on long holidays, pool and water park get crowded
Quality of meals other than breakfast is inconsistent (per reviews)
Soundproofing between rooms may not be enough for light sleepers

entries.name: Homey Dormy Chiangrai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Rop Wiang·near Central Plaza · 10 min walk to the mall
entries.addr: 147 Moo 13 Phaholyothin Road, Rop Wiang, Mueang Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: If you're tired of big chain hotels that look the same in every city, and you want a small place where the owner remembers your face from day one, Homey Dormy Chiangrai is a name travelers mention with a smile. It's a family-run boutique B&B with just 12 rooms, in the Rop Wiang area on Phaholyothin Road, about 700 meters from Central Plaza Chiang Rai, roughly a 10-minute walk, with the mall, restaurants, a cinema, and a supermarket within walking distance. The whole charm is the personal attention — many guests say it feels like "staying at a relative's house in Chiang Rai" because the owner and the team look after it closely themselves, remember guests' names, and give local tips on what to see and eat. What reviews agree on is that the rooms are spotless and bigger than the price suggests — many use the words sparkling clean — and the fresh breakfast changes every day with no repeats, Western, American, and Asian, which the owner asks about and adjusts to order. The hot-water shower also draws special praise for genuinely strong, hot water. There are free bikes and free private parking, good if you drive yourself. The honest caveats: it's on the outskirts, about 2 kilometers from the old town and Clock Tower, so without a car you'll need to call a Grab to head into town in the evening; there's no pool; and the place has stairs, not convenient for anyone with limited mobility or heavy luggage. Best for couples, solo travelers, and small families who drive themselves and value peace and quiet, from around ฿700/night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you don't have a car, budget for a Grab into town in the evening, or use the free bikes to Central Plaza and nearby areas. If you want a spacious room or one with a balcony, book early — there are only 12 rooms and they fill fast in winter — and tell them your arrival time if you're coming late, since there's no 24-hour front desk.
pros: Warm, family-run service, owner looks after it personally and remembers names
Spotless rooms bigger than the price, strong hot-water shower
Fresh breakfast made daily with changing menu, adjusted on request
Free bikes and parking, 10-minute walk to Central Plaza
cons: On the outskirts, about 2 km from the old town, not so convenient without a car
No pool, gym, or spa
Has stairs and no 24-hour front desk

entries.name: Na-Rak-O Resort
entries.badge: 🎨 Cute as the name says · walk to the Night Bazaar
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sanpanoi·downtown · 350 m walk to the Night Bazaar
tags: 🎨 Bright, colorful decor, great for photos
🌃 350 m walk to the Night Bazaar
entries.addr: 56 Sanpanard Soi 2/1, Wiang, Mueang Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: Picture a small, brightly colored stay tucked away on a quiet soi in central Chiang Rai, a few minutes' walk from the Night Bazaar and the Clock Tower that changes color at night — Na-Rak-O Resort, with the Thai name Na-Rak-O ("so cute") Resort, is the budget boutique stay many people talk about as living up to its cute name. It's a small property with 24 rooms, opened in 2014 and renovated in 2016, scoring 9.1 from 43 reviews on Trip.com, which is remarkably high for a stay of just a few hundred baht. The clearest strength is the location — it's "close to everything but not chaotic" — a few minutes' walk to the Chiang Rai Night Bazaar and Wat Jed Yod (about 350 meters), about 800 meters' walk to the Chiang Rai Clock Tower, and within walking distance of the old central bus station, very convenient if you arrive by bus. The charm everyone mentions is the bright, colorful decor where each room has its own character and photographs well, and the staff who look after you like family. There's a free shared kitchen and common seating area, good if you want to cook or make coffee, plus free parking and luggage storage. The honest caveats: it's a small building so soundproofing between rooms isn't perfect — light sleepers should pack earplugs — the shower curtain in some rooms is rather short so water splashes onto the floor, and there's no pool or gym. Best for budget travelers, couples, and small families who want a cute place in a walkable downtown spot, from around ฿600/night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Make the most of the location — a few minutes' walk to the Night Bazaar and the Clock Tower that changes color at night, so you can head out for good food and walk back easily. If you sleep lightly, pack earplugs and ask for a room not next to the corridor, and if you're driving, open a map to find the entrance to Sanpanoi Soi 2/1, since the soi is narrow and the sign isn't big.
pros: Downtown location, walk to the Night Bazaar, Clock Tower, and bus station
Bright, colorful decor that photographs well, each room with its own character
Free shared kitchen and parking · kind, helpful staff
Great value among downtown budget stays
cons: Small building, soundproofing between rooms isn't perfect
No pool, gym, or elevator
Short shower curtain in some rooms, water splashes onto the floor (per reviews)

entries.name: The Rama Hotel
entries.badge: 🛏️ Rooms bigger than the price · near the airport
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Rop Wiang·near downtown · 12 min to the airport
tags: 🛏️ Rooms bigger than the price, several pillow types
🚗 Free parking, 7 km from the airport
entries.addr: 217/1 Moo 19, Rop Wiang, Mueang Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: In the Rop Wiang area just a kilometer from central Chiang Rai, there's a small, simple hotel that mid-budget travelers talk about for value — The Rama Hotel. It's a 3-star city hotel with around 30 rooms that sells value rather than luxury. We have to say it straight: the overall score of 7.8 from 27 reviews on Trip.com and Tripadvisor 4.1 out of 5 isn't as high as the others in this article — it's not a hotel everyone falls for flawlessly, but it's an option a fair number of people are happy with for the price they pay. What reviews mention most and agree on across nearly every platform is that the rooms are clearly bigger than what you pay — many are surprised they pay a few hundred baht and get a room this open and comfortable, with several types of pillows to choose from and a bed that's just firm enough. Another praised point is the service — the service score on Trip.com is around 8.1, higher than the overall score, and reviews mention friendly staff who are helpful with car rental, tour booking, and airport transfers. The location has the advantage of being close to Mae Fah Luang Airport, about 6.8 kilometers or 12 minutes by car, and there's free parking. The honest caveats: there's no pool, some rooms are starting to show age and there are reviews of water leaks in the bathroom, cleanliness is inconsistent in places, and the location means a drive or a crossing of a big road to get into town — it's not a walk-to-the-Night-Bazaar area. Best for mid-budget couples, small families, and anyone driving around Chiang Rai who uses the hotel as a base, from around ฿450/night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check clearly on the booking page whether your chosen rate includes breakfast, since the info differs across platforms. Check the room and bathroom at check-in, especially for water leaks, and if you find something that needs fixing, report it right away to ask for a room change, and book the airport transfer ahead since it's a paid service.
pros: Rooms bigger than the price, clean, comfortable, several pillow types
Friendly staff, service category scores highest
Free parking, about 7 km from Mae Fah Luang Airport (12 min by car)
Very affordable, from around ฿450/night
cons: No pool
Some rooms starting to show age, reviews of water leaks in the bathroom
Location requires a drive into town, not a walk-to-the-Night-Bazaar area

entries.name: Baanmalai Guest House
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.3 · Tripadvisor 4.6/5 from 249 reviews · Travelers' Choice
entries.badge: 🧼 Rooms cleaner than the price · walk to the Night Bazaar
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wiang sub-district·quiet downtown soi · 5–10 min walk to the Night Bazaar
tags: 🧼 Rooms clean and bigger than the price
🚶 5–10 min walk to the Night Bazaar
entries.addr: 32/2 Moo 18, Soi Sanpanao, Wiang, Mueang Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: Picture a two-story house on a quiet soi in central Chiang Rai, with a small garden out front, the owner coming out to greet you from the first step, hot coffee poured for free in the lobby, and rooms that are spacious and cleaner than the price — that's Baanmalai Guest House, or Baan Malai Guest House. It's a small guesthouse with around 15 rooms that the owner's family runs hands-on, open since 2012, on Soi Sanpanoi in the Wiang area in the center, scoring 9.3 from 86 reviews on Trip.com and Tripadvisor 4.6/5 from 249 reviews with a Travelers' Choice award (#5 of 162 specialty stays in Chiang Rai). The selling point reviews agree on most is the hard-to-find location — a central area but a fairly quiet, safe soi, about a 5–10 minute walk to the Night Bazaar, the Walking Street, and the bus station, a little farther to the Clock Tower. The most-praised point is the cleanliness of the rooms — many use the word superclean — and rooms bigger than the price, with comfortable beds, paired with free tea and coffee 24 hours in the lobby and the owner's family-style care. Breakfast is simple but the coffee is good and there's an egg station where they fry eggs to order. The honest caveats: the building is a house with no elevator, so upper-floor rooms mean carrying luggage up the stairs; soundproofing between rooms isn't perfect; and there's no pool or gym. Best for couples, solo travelers, and small families who want a clean room, a central location, and genuine care, from around ฿600/night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Use it as a base for walking to the Night Bazaar, the Walking Street, and the Clock Tower, and head out for local Lanna food every evening. If you have heavy luggage or struggle with stairs, ask for a ground-floor room at booking since there's no elevator, and check the breakfast terms clearly since some rates may not include it.
pros: Very clean rooms (superclean) and bigger than the price, comfortable beds
Downtown location, walk to the Night Bazaar and Walking Street, but a quiet, safe soi
Family-run by the owner · Tripadvisor 4.6/5, Travelers' Choice award
Free tea & coffee 24 hours, Wi-Fi, and free parking
cons: No elevator, upper-floor rooms mean walking up the stairs
Soundproofing between rooms and from outside isn't perfect
Simple amenities, no pool or gym

entries.type: Budget 2-Star · Luxury Economy with a pool
entries.name: Pimanninn
entries.revCount: Trip.com 7.9 · many reviews · Pimann Inn Hotel
entries.badge: 💸 A pool at a budget price · spacious parking
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Rop Wiang·in town · 1.9 km from the Clock Tower
tags: 🏊 Pool open till midnight + gym + sauna
entries.addr: 652/1 Moo 24, Rob Wiang, Mueang Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: If budget is the main concern but you still want a pool, a gym, and a spacious clean room, Pimanninn (some sites write it Pimann Inn Hotel) is a name that comes up often in Chiang Rai. It's a large budget hotel with 150+ rooms that positions itself as a "Luxury Economy Hotel" — the straightforward idea is to cut the extras to keep the price low, but still give you more than the price suggests. To be honest, the overall score of around 7.9 isn't as high as the others, and it's not a flawless hotel, but its whole stance is pure "value for money." The number-one strength that keeps it on the list is the large outdoor pool that stays open until midnight — few hotels at this price have a real pool to swim in, open this late — paired with a gym, sauna, massage room, and very spacious free parking, which is what people driving around Chiang Rai like most. Rooms are bigger than expected for the price, and many have a private balcony. The caveat we have to state straight is the location — the hotel's site says "city center," but it's actually about 1.9 km from the Chiang Rai Clock Tower and about 2.5 km from the Night Bazaar. One review describes it as "too far to walk but too close to call a car" — very comfortable with your own car, but without one you'll rely on Grab every time. On top of that, room quality is inconsistent, some rooms have old furniture or a musty smell, and breakfast leans Asian with few Western options. Best for budget travelers driving themselves who want a pool to cool off in, from around ฿750/night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Driving yourself works best here, since the parking is spacious and free and the location needs a car — use it as a base for Wat Rong Khun and the Black House. Ask for a recently renovated room at booking since room quality is inconsistent, and use the pool in the evening, since it's open until midnight and there are sometimes kids' swimming classes during the day.
pros: Genuinely budget, Luxury Economy concept, from around ฿750/night
Has a pool open till midnight, a gym, and a sauna — more than most hotels at this price
Very spacious free parking, convenient if you drive yourself
Rooms bigger than expected, many with a balcony
cons: Location about 2–3 km from the Clock Tower and Night Bazaar, needs a car into town
Some bathrooms and furniture are old, room quality is inconsistent
Breakfast leans Asian, few Western options

entries.name: The Legend Chiang Rai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Kok riverside·Rim Kok · 5 min to town
tags: 🏞️ Kok riverside, bird garden with 50 species
🍽️ Riverside Sala Rim Nam + La Casa
entries.addr: 124/15 Moo 21 Kohloy Road, Rim Kok, Mueang Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: We close the list with a riverside resort many people overlook — if you want a quiet riverside resort atmosphere with a garden, birds, and a pool looking out over the Kok River, but don't want to drive far out of town, The Legend Chiang Rai Boutique River Resort & Spa is the answer. It's a 4-star boutique resort with 76 rooms and pool villas in contemporary Lanna style, on the Kok River in the Rim Kok area, scoring 9.2 from 1,442 reviews — the most reviews among the riverside resorts in this article. What sets it apart from the downtown hotels is the quiet Kok-riverside location that's still only about a 5-minute drive from town and the Chiang Rai Clock Tower, about 7 minutes from the Night Bazaar, and about 8 kilometers from the airport. The most-mentioned highlight is the infinity pool on the Kok River, where the pool's edge flows on into the line of the river, with a jacuzzi and a kids' pool, paired with a garden that over 50 species of local birds visit — lots come out in the early morning, and many guests like to stroll the garden with a coffee. Rooms start at the Superior Studio, which is spacious and has a semi-outdoor bathroom paved with natural stone, like bathing in the garden. The breakfast buffet at the riverside Sala Rim Nam also gets plenty of praise, and there's La Casa, a wood-fired Italian, for a special meal. The honest caveats: the resort has been open a long time, so some of the building and furniture is starting to show wear; food and spa prices at the resort run rather high; the pool water temperature is chilly on some winter days; there are mosquitoes in the garden during the rainy season; and you always need a car into town. Best for couples and anyone who wants a quiet riverside escape at a more affordable price than the other luxury riverside resorts, from around ฿2,300/night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a riverside room (River View) or the Grand Deluxe for views of the Kok River and the morning mist in winter. Stroll the bird garden in the early morning when lots of birds come out and the air is just right; resort food prices are high, so drive the 5 minutes into town to the Night Bazaar or local restaurants now and then, and bring mosquito repellent if you come in the rainy season.
pros: Quiet on the Kok River, bird garden with 50 species, yet 5 minutes to town
Riverside infinity pool with a jacuzzi and kids' pool
Spacious Lanna rooms, semi-outdoor bathroom · praised riverside breakfast
More affordable than the other luxury riverside resorts in Chiang Rai
cons: Open a long time, some of the building and furniture starting to show wear
Food and spa prices at the resort run rather high · always need a car into town
Pool temperature chilly on some winter days · mosquitoes in the garden in the rainy season

adviceTitle: How do you pick a hotel in Chiang Rai city to match your trip?

advice.head: Want a riverside escape with a brand you can trust
advice.bodyHtml: → Le Meridien Chiang Rai Resort ฿3,500, a Marriott resort on the Kok River, 26-rai garden, riverside pool, warm service, 10 minutes to town and the airport

advice.head: Traveling with kids, want a water park
advice.bodyHtml: → The Riverie by Katathani ฿2,600, a Kok-riverside resort in the center, The River Splash water park, kids' club, rooftop with a city view, Tripadvisor #2

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard-room range and may change by date and season. We recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking. The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves. The winter season (November–February) has the most pleasant cool weather and the prettiest river views, but it's high season, so prices rise and rooms fill fast — book ahead. Chiang Rai has no metro; use Grab, songthaew, or rent a car, and it's about 10–20 minutes from Mae Fah Luang Airport into town. Riverside resorts need a car into town, while downtown hotels and guesthouses are within walking distance of the Night Bazaar and the Walking Street. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travelers often ask about hotels in Chiang Rai city

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best hotel in Chiang Rai city?
faq.a: It depends on your style of trip. By score, Le Patta Hotel Chiang Rai at 9.6 is the highest in this article, a downtown boutique with free snacks all day. For a luxury riverside resort with a water park for kids, The Riverie by Katathani, Tripadvisor #2. For service and quiet on the river, Le Meridien Chiang Rai Resort, in the Marriott group. To explore downtown on foot, Nak Nakara. And for a clean room at a great price, Baanmalai Guest House or Homey Dormy.

faq.q: ❓ How much do hotels in Chiang Rai city cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start from around ฿450–3,500 per night. On the budget side: The Rama from ฿450, Na-Rak-O and Baanmalai from ฿600, Homey Dormy ฿700, and Pimanninn ฿750. Mid-range: Le Patta ฿1,100 and Nak Nakara ฿1,500. And at the resort level: The Legend ฿2,300, The Riverie ฿2,600, and Le Meridien ฿3,500. All prices are approximate starting prices for standard rooms, and they may run higher in winter and over festivals.

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Chiang Rai city?
faq.a: Kok riverside (the Rop Wiang / Rim Kok area) suits anyone who wants a quiet resort with a river view and a pool, but you need a car into town (Le Meridien, The Riverie, The Legend). Downtown (Wiang sub-district) suits anyone who wants to walk to the Walking Street, Night Bazaar, and restaurants without a car (Nak Nakara, Le Patta, Na-Rak-O, Baanmalai). The Rop Wiang area / near Central Plaza suits anyone driving themselves, close to the airport, quiet (Homey Dormy, The Rama, Pimanninn).

faq.q: ❓ Which hotel in Chiang Rai city is good for families with children?
faq.a: The best fit is The Riverie by Katathani, with The River Splash water park with slides, a kids' zone, and a kids' club — children can play all day. Next are Le Meridien and The Legend, with pools and big gardens for kids to run around by the Kok River. In town on a budget, Nak Nakara has a separate kids' pool and a walkable location, and Pimanninn has a pool at a budget price.

faq.q: ❓ Coming to Chiang Rai without a car, where should I stay?
faq.a: If you don't have your own car, choose a hotel or guesthouse downtown (Wiang sub-district) within walking distance of the Night Bazaar, the Walking Street, and the bus station. Good options are Le Patta (100 meters from the Walking Street), Nak Nakara (3-minute walk to the Walking Street), Baanmalai, and Na-Rak-O (walk to the Night Bazaar). The riverside resorts and the stays in the Rop Wiang area like Le Meridien, The Riverie, The Legend, Homey Dormy, The Rama, and Pimanninn need a car into town.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Chiang Rai hotel?
faq.a: During high season (November–February), with pleasant cool weather and festivals, book 1–2 months ahead, especially the riverside resorts and small stays like Homey Dormy (12 rooms), Baanmalai (~15 rooms), and Na-Rak-O (24 rooms), which have few rooms and fill fast. Other times, 2–3 weeks is enough. Every platform has Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in a rate like that if your plans aren't firm yet, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
